quizzes.stem: A team wants every reply from Claude Sonnet 5.5 to be a record in a fixed JSON shape. What does the documentation recommend?

options.a: Structured outputs with the schema in the output configuration
options.b: A forced tool whose schema is the record, chosen with the name field
options.c: A prompt that shows the record and asks the model to copy the shape
options.d: A tool choice of any, so that some tool is always called

explanation.a: The page says to use structured outputs "when you need a response in a fixed JSON shape".
explanation.b: Ruled out because `any` and `tool` "return a 400 error" on Claude Sonnet 5.5.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a prompt gives "no guarantee; the program must parse defensively".
explanation.d: Ruled out because `any` is one of the values that "return a 400 error" on this model.

quizzes.stem: The schema says a field named `total` has a `minimum` of 0, and the request is sent with that schema unchanged. What happens?

options.a: It fails with a 400 error that gives details
options.b: The reply is checked against the limit and retried for the caller
options.c: The limit is read as a hint and the call goes on as usual
options.d: The constraint is applied only when the field is a whole number

explanation.a: The page says "If you use an unsupported feature, you'll receive a 400 error with details."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a helper that validates responses still enforces every constraint in your code", so the check is the program's job.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "If you use an unsupported feature" the outcome is an error, with no hint read.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the numerical constraints are listed as unsupported with no exception: "Numerical constraints (such as `minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`)".

quizzes.stem: A reply arrives with a 200 status and `stop_reason` of `refusal`. What should the program assume about the body?

options.a: The refusal message takes the place of the promised shape
options.b: It keeps the shape, because the status code says success
options.c: It becomes whole once the call is repeated with more tokens
options.d: It is always an empty object, which signals the refusal

explanation.a: The page says "The output may not match your schema because the refusal message takes precedence over schema constraints."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a refusal has "a 200 status code and billed tokens" and still breaks the shape.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the remedy of more tokens belongs to `max_tokens`: "Retry with a higher `max_tokens` value to get the complete structured output."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page names no such body, only that the output "may not match your schema".

quizzes.stem: A reply arrives as a friendly sentence, then JSON inside a code block, then a closing remark. Which reading order does the page give?

options.a: Reject the whole reply, since extra words around the data are not allowed
options.b: Strip only the leading sentence, then parse whatever text is left over
options.c: The first fence's body, else the span from the first brace to the last
options.d: Parse the last line alone, since data tends to follow the prose in a reply

explanation.c: The page's steps are to take the first fence's body, then "the span from the first `{` to the last `}`".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the reader "repairs a harmless habit" of wrapping the data in words.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the steps start from the fence or the braces: "If the text has a code fence, take the body of the first fence".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the steps name no position for the data, only "Take the span from the first `{` to the last `}`".

quizzes.stem: A validator meets `true` where the schema wants an integer quantity. What does the page decide?

options.a: Accept it, since in many languages a truthy value counts as the number one
options.b: Convert it to 1 and go on with the remaining checks of the field
options.c: One problem for the value, and no further checks of it
options.d: Report a separate problem for every constraint that the field carries in the schema

explanation.c: The page says "A wrong type stops the checks of that value." and "`true` is not a quantity".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A boolean is never a number or an integer".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the reader "does not repair a broken value", and the same holds for a value.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A wrong type stops the checks of that value", so no further problem is added.

quizzes.stem: Which result ends the extractor loop without another call to the model?

options.a: A reply with a valid body but a total of zero, which breaks the minimum
options.b: A reply that quotes a sentence which the document never contained
options.c: A reply whose JSON is wrapped in a code fence with prose around it
options.d: A reply cut off at the token limit

explanation.d: The page says a reply at the limit has the action "Raise `max_tokens` or continue the response", and that "Asking again with an error list cannot fix either".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the validator "returns a list of problems, each with a path", and the next call uses it.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a failed check leads to a repair: "the next call needs the whole conversation".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "If the text has a code fence, take the body of the first fence", so the reply is read and not rejected.

quizzes.stem: An invoice extractor runs on a model that supports structured outputs. The reply has the right fields and types, yet the cited sentence is one the document never contained. Who catches it?

options.a: The API, because the schema lists the evidence field as a string type
options.b: Only the program, by searching the source for that wording
options.c: The grammar cache, which compares each reply with the earlier replies
options.d: The stop reason, which flags every invented sentence at the end of the reply

explanation.b: The page says "If the string is not in the document, the model made it up or changed it", and the check "needs no model".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A schema cannot say that a number is at least 0, that a quotation occurs in the document".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the cache only holds a compiled grammar: "Compiled grammars are cached for 24 hours from last use".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The loop reads `stop_reason` before the body", and it reports why generation ended, not whether the text is true.

quizzes.stem: A team's code retries every failed reply up to five times. A document triggers a `refusal`. What is the right change?

options.a: Raise the attempts to ten, so that one of the later calls gets past it
options.b: Add the refusal text to the next prompt, for the model to explain itself
options.c: Switch to a forced tool, which accepts every document without objection
options.d: Stop there, report it, and issue no further call

explanation.d: The page says a `refusal` has the action "Read `stop_details` and retry on a fallback model.", and that "a refusal is a decision, not a malformed answer".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The same request gets the same decision, and each call is billed."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Asking again with an error list cannot fix either".
explanation.c: Ruled out because on some models `any` and `tool` "return a 400 error", and no tool choice overrides a refusal.

quizzes.stem: A schema has an enum of `USD`, `EUR` and `GBP`, and a reply returns `Eur`. How should the program treat it?

options.a: As a schema violation, since the characters differ from the allowed list
options.b: As a match, ignoring capital letters when comparing
options.c: As an API error, reported with a 400 status code on the request
options.d: As a refusal, because the promised shape was not honoured by the model

explanation.b: The page says "Compare enum values case-insensitively, and avoid enum values that differ only in capitalization."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the response completes normally, "with no error and no special `stop_reason`", and the difference is only in capital letters.
explanation.c: is ruled out for the same reason, since the response is "with no error and no special `stop_reason`".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A refusal is a result to report", and it is marked by its stop reason, which this reply lacks.

quizzes.stem: A reply with `stop_reason` of `max_tokens` holds `{"vendor": "Acme`. Which step should the program take?

options.a: Close the braces itself and validate the value it guessed from the text
options.b: Report it as truncated and raise the limit
options.c: Re-prompt with the error list, so that the model finishes the missing text
options.d: Treat it as a refusal and switch over to a fallback model for the retry

explanation.b: The page says "Raise `max_tokens` or continue the response", and "The reader repairs a harmless habit. It does not repair a broken value".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "guessing missing braces turns a cut-off reply into a wrong record".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Asking again with an error list cannot fix either: a cut-off reply needs a larger limit".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a refusal is a decision, not a malformed answer", and a cut-off reply is a different stop reason.
